titleStmt.title: Excavated texts 简牍 · 秦庄襄王元年: notes

div.interp: The first year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, 249 BC, whom the Chronicle calls King Zhuang; the year is given with no entry under it.

泰上皇, that is 太上皇, the title the First Emperor gave his father King Zhuangxiang after his death; "in the time of" the Grand Supreme Emperor is Zhuangxiang's reign, 249–247 BC, which places the statute here, at the reign's first year; the year within the reign is not given.

践更: the editors' pause marks make three groups, sikou, yinguan and men on their geng turn; Chen Wei reads 司寇、隐官践更, the sikou and yinguan on their geng turn, as in another Yuelu statute (slip 017). The editors' punctuation is kept.
议: the ruling that answers the report (言); the form of a Qin statute of this kind.
入禾: grain unhusked; the County supplies the grain its sikou will eat at the Workshop.
貣, the editors' reading 贷 kept in parentheses: 当貣者, the quantity due to be lent.
作所县: the County in which the Workshop's work-site lies.
偿及贷: as read here, the County of the work-site lends the grain and the sikou's own County repays it.
听…致: 致, the note by which an office calls for men or goods to be delivered; 听, to comply with it.
移: the forwarding of men and of the papers that go with them.
·二年曰：复用: an annotation after the scribe's dot, recording that the statute was put back in force in a second year; Chen Wei takes it as the second year of King Zheng, 245 BC.
泰上皇元年: the Suiji, a Han text, calls King Zhuangxiang by the title given him after his death (see §2); 249 BC.
立三年: the reign summed up at its first year, as the Suiji does for each ruler; 249–247 BC.
生始皇帝: that the king was the First Emperor's father, not that the First Emperor was born this year (the Shiji puts his birth in 259 BC).
呂不韋相: his appointment as Chancellor of State is in the Basic Annals for this year, §1.
The entry goes on; the rest of it is not reproduced here.

The text names neither the king nor the year. The excavation report (Li Tianhong and others, Wenwu 2022/3) takes the king to be King Zhuangxiang and the occasion the five-state alliance of his third year, 247 BC; the text is placed here, at the first year of the reign. The parenthesised readings are the editors'; □ marks a lost graph and …… a lost stretch; 正1 to 背6 number the lines, seven on the front of the tablet and six on the back.
王之外訄臣筡: 訄, to press; read here as the petitioner from outside the court pressing his suit. The graph after 筡 is read 愿 by the editors.
倚立之閒（闲）: the pause of a king standing, that is a short audience.
渴（竭）腹之所闻: to exhaust what his belly holds of what he has heard.
衍: unexplained; it stands where a state is expected and may be 燕 Yan, the two graphs being near in sound. Left as a name.
五邦: the five states allied against Qin; the report takes them as the Wei, Zhao, Han, Chu and Yan of Lord Xinling's alliance of 247 BC.
陟＝若壹: the ＝ is the scribe's repetition mark, 陟陟, to advance; as one.
甗, read 献 by the editors: to present terms.
刀居（锯）: the knife and the saw, the instruments of punishment.
以不义反为义: the refrain of the speech; 反 as "turned", unrighteousness turned into righteousness in their own eyes.

巍（魏）人与越人战宿胥之壄（野）: the received histories know no battle of Wei and Yue at Suxu, which lay on the Yellow River in Wei; what follows, the King of Yue perched on Kuaiji, is the Wu siege of Goujian of 494 BC. The text is left as it stands.
廥（会）稽廥纂之上: 廥纂 after 会稽 is unexplained; read as the heights of the mountain.
侵, read 寝 by the editors: 寝兵, to lay arms to rest.
强为天子: Wu's claim to lead the Lords under King Fuchai, as at the meeting of Huangchi.
及与大都连者: the lands adjoining the great capital.
有（蚀）寒之色: the editors read the graph as 蚀 and take the phrase as the look of gaunt hunger and cold; Wang Ning would read 饥 outright.
壹恶用兵矣: 壹 as the intensifier, how greatly.
酆綦: not identified; the readings proposed are 逢忌, the marsh of Fengji near Daliang (Lin Xiaoyang), and 豐析 (Xie Minghong). Left as a name.
斩首六矣: the unit of the six is not given; six campaigns, or six (tens of thousands of) heads.
佴, read 耻 by the editors.
皆未罢也: 罢, to be released from service; the soldiers have never been relieved. The sentence recurs as a refrain of the swords and the horse.
金试□兔（？）壶（？）□□□□□……□勿绎（释）: the sentence on the swords is largely lost; 绎, read 释 by the editors, to let go, as of the horse below.
骀马: a broken-down horse; the finest horse, never rested, ends a nag.
王之（禄）也: the editors read the graph as 禄, emolument.
绳身: literally to cord the body; read as to bind themselves to the service that costs them 断剅（头）列（裂）腹, heads cut off and bellies ripped.
宛取□□身以（迁）徙忧守之: the graph read 迁 by the editors; the people moved to hold new land in anxious guard.
约车众者数百[乘]: 乘 supplied by the editors in brackets; 约车, to bind oneself to furnish chariots.
责阵卒: the sense of the sentence is lost with its seven graphs.
兴而治地，地方环（圆）不□百余里: the land won by a campaign, a hundred-odd li round, must be peopled from the interior (中□之民).
且茗: 茗 unexplained.
允其图（？）□: the editors' reading, queried by them.
陈责皆赏: 陈责, old debts or arrears; 赏 as read, rewarded, or remitted.
黄啻□曰行年三百□椯（端）身□察乃智（知）足: 黄啻 is the Yellow Emperor (啻 for 帝); the saying is broken by two lost graphs; 椯 read 端 by the editors.

东南囊（？）楚而北半赵: the editors query 囊; Qin's land enclosing Chu to the south-east and taking half of Zhao to the north, after the fall of Ying in 278 BC and Changping in 260 BC. 膏 supplied by the editors in brackets.
到无甲之□: the far west where no armour is worn; the graph lost.
最奡: the editors read 奡 as 豪, the porcupine; Wang Ning reads 獒, a dog; Fang Yong reads the graph as 戛, 最戛 for 丛棘, thickets of jujube; Cai Wei reads 獿 and Xie Minghong 狙猱, the macaque. Romanised.
必方: the editors read 苾芳, fragrant plants, and note the bird 畢方; Fang Yong reads 枋, a tree. Romanised.
婴（樱）母（梅）: the editors' reading; Wang Ning reads 鹦鹉, the parrot, as the Shijing commentary writes it.
鐘蠪胥（蹇）之州: 鐘蠪 read 籦籠, a bamboo (Bing Shangbai); 胥蹇 likewise a bamboo; 州 as islet.
赣勒: read 瑊玏, a stone like jade (Cai Wei). Romanised.
敝稯（椶）、桃支（枝）: 敝椶 the palm (栟櫚), 桃枝 a bamboo.
